inputs.share_count_basis: 4,319.334m shares on issue, unchanged every year FY2016-H1 FY2026; no share options or awards outstanding (FY2025 AR: 'The Group does not have any share option'), so basic = fully diluted. Held flat; no buybacks despite the 10% repurchase mandate.
inputs.net_cash_composition: 30 June 2026 interim balance sheet (RMB m): long-term time deposits 5,034.7 + short-term time deposits 5,535.0 + cash and cash equivalents 1,609.9 + restricted cash 1.0 = 12,180.5 gross; company's own net-cash definition excludes accrued interest receivable, giving 11,880.0 (H1 FY2026 MD&A net cash 9,324.0 + total borrowings incl. leases 2,555.9). Plus FVTPL structured bank deposits 1,611.7 (principal-protected, maturing within 12 months) = cash 13,491.7. Debt = unsecured bank borrowings 2,516.1 + lease liabilities 39.8 = 2,555.9. The FY2025 final dividend of 2,050.6 was declared and sitting in other payables at 30 June (paid 8 July 2026) and is deducted in equity_bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment scheme: FY2025 Annual Report states the Group has no share option scheme; EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year. SBC-zero market treatment (owner-fcf-adaptations e).
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. Per-share values computed in CNY and converted at CNYHKD 1.1721 (Yahoo Finance CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-10T03:38Z). No dual listing exists for a parity check; magnitude check: FY2025 EPS RMB0.4747 x 1.1721 = HK$0.556, P/E 13.8x at the quote, in line with the 14-15x HK-listed China staples range.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:05Z regular close (Yahoo regularMarketTime; Friday close, market shut over weekend)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY: China 10y government bond ~1.9% + China equity risk premium ~7.0% x beta ~0.85 (defensive staple, HK-listed China consumer) = ~7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. All-equity: borrowings are short-term working-capital lines dwarfed by cash. Same WACC in all scenarios; competitive and commodity risk is carried in the scenario flows, not stacked on the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities (RMB39.8m) included in total_debt; lease principal (RMB30m FY2025) NOT deducted from flows. Right-of-use amortisation (RMB78m, mostly prepaid land-use rights) sits in D&A. Immaterial either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: profit for the year equals profit attributable to equity holders (no non-controlling interests).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (scenario-weighted) per dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US: consumer' plus the adaptations file - this is a PRC instant-noodle and RTD-beverage manufacturer, not a financial, REIT or holdco. FY0 anchors (FY2025 AR, RMB m): revenue 31,714.3; operating profit 2,565.0; D&A 1,088.2 (PP&E 982.7 + ROU 78.1 + investment property 24.7 + intangibles 2.8) -> EBITDA 3,653.3 = 11.5% margin; capex 1,084.5 (3.4%); income tax 700.7 on PBT 2,750.9 (25.5%), cash tax paid 769.7. Owner FCF = OCF 3,284.4 - capex 1,084.5 - SBC 0 - interest income 257.3 = 1,942.5. Interest income stripped because the matching ~RMB13.5bn cash/deposit/structured-deposit pile is added in the bridge (net cash ~5.6x the FCF base). EBITDA here is operating profit + D&A, so it excludes finance income and the equity-method share (FY2025 loss 47.9, FY2024 profit 59.4); the equity-method investments (RMB760.2m at 30 June 2026) therefore go into the bridge at book. Structured-deposit FV gains (~RMB15-40m) sit inside 'other gains' in operating profit and are a minor double count left in. Working capital: distributors prepay (contract liabilities RMB4.1bn at December), so net working capital is negative and growth releases a little cash; wc_capture set at a conservative +5% of the revenue increase. Contract liabilities are strongly seasonal (4,096 at Dec vs 1,470 at June) - the June net-cash anchor therefore does NOT include the year-end distributor-prepayment float, which makes it the conservative vintage. Buybacks: zero; the flat count is natural, not funded, since there is no SBC. Dividend payout ~100% of profit (FY2025 DPS RMB0.4747 = EPS).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-0.4% 5yr, 1.0% 3yr) diverges >30% from revenue (6.9%/3.9%) and EPS (4.8%/18.8%) CAGRs. This is structural, not a data problem: the company pays out ~100% of profit, so book value cannot compound. Equity CAGR is rejected as the growth proxy; the 3-year revenue CAGR is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - interest income (SBC is zero). 3yr owner-FCF CAGR of 39.5% starts from the FY2022 trough (owner FCF 715.5 when input-cost inflation and COVID lockdowns compressed margins and working capital unwound); 5yr CAGR of -6.1% starts from the FY2020 peak (2,663.3, a COVID at-home-consumption windfall with EBITDA margin 14.9%). Neither endpoint is a fair trend; the base case anchors on FY2025 components instead. Owner-FCF CAGRs sit below reported-FCF CAGRs only because interest income is stripped - there is no SBC drag.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +3% (H1 +1.4% with food +4.7% and beverages flat; H2 comps easier). Mid-single-digit growth thereafter from noodle premiumisation and isotonic/sugar-free beverage lines offsetting tea/juice decline, fading to 2%. EBITDA margin steps from 11.5% to 12.0% on the H1 gross-margin gain (35.0% vs 34.3%) and holds ~12.3%, inside the FY2020-25 range of 9.3-14.9%. Capex ~D&A. Cash tax 27% = 25% PRC CIT plus dividend withholding leakage to the HK/Cayman parent.

scenario_narratives.base: Steady #2 in a concentrated China instant-noodle market: premium SKUs (Tang Daren soup noodles, Lao Tan, Sam's Club co-creations) keep food growing mid-single digits while isotonic and sugar-free lines roughly offset declining tea and juice in the 62%-of-revenue beverage segment. Neither Uni-President nor Master Kong raises list prices, so margin gains come from mix only and plateau around 12.3% EBITDA. Revenue compounds ~3% for a decade and essentially all owner FCF is paid out.
scenario_narratives.bull: Premiumisation keeps working and the China consumer recovers moderately: food grows high-single digits, sports/isotonic drinks and new occasions (banquet, gifting, instant retail) return beverages to growth, and Baixiang's share gains stall as reported in 2026. Mix plus a benign palm-oil/wheat/PET cost backdrop lift EBITDA margin back toward the FY2020-21 13-14% band. Revenue ~5% CAGR over five years.
scenario_narratives.bear: Low-cost challenger Baixiang keeps taking noodle share (5.9% in 2021 to ~15% in 2025, against Uni-President's ~18%), forcing promotional spend, while tea and juice keep shrinking and health trends erode both traditional noodles and sugared drinks. A palm-oil or wheat spike cannot be passed through under the industry's no-price-rise stance, so EBITDA margin slides to 10% - near the FY2022 9.3% trough - and revenue barely grows.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): an identifiable, already-visible share threat from Baixiang plus commodity exposure with no pricing power, though the RMB10.9bn net-cash balance sheet removes any solvency tail. Base 55%: a decade-long record of mid-single-digit growth and ~100% payout makes the steady path the modal outcome. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs several independent things - consumer recovery, beverage turnaround, benign input costs and stalled competitor share gains - to go right at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A mature, cash-rich China staples franchise valued on owner FCF: operating cash generation after capex, with interest on the RMB13.5bn deposit pile stripped out of the flows and the pile itself (net of borrowings, leases and the declared-but-unpaid dividend) added in the bridge. No SBC, so house and street bases coincide. Roughly a third of the market capitalisation is net cash, and with ~100% payout the investment case is essentially a dividend stream plus that cash.
key_risks_to_valuation: Baixiang Food share gains at the value end of instant noodles force price or promotion responses that the base margin path does not include
Beverages are 62% of revenue and tea/juice are declining; isotonic growth may not offset them
Palm oil, wheat and PET cost spikes with no pricing power (both leaders have publicly resisted price rises)
Cash is held in PRC bank deposits; it is only fully accessible to HK shareholders after PRC dividend withholding tax and continued 100% payout. A change in payout policy would trap value
Related-party dependency on parent Uni-President Enterprises (2026 framework purchase agreement through 2029)
RMB/HKD exchange-rate moves translate directly into the HKD value
